thread:
Rafael Mendes: heads up, we just pushed a *test* perf-canary regression alert through the new route. can folks sanity check payload + links? (this is from us-east, llama-3.1-8b-instruct slice)

incident-bot: *[TEST]* Perf Canary Regression Detected (p95_latency)
service: perf-canary
severity: SEV-3 (test)
model: llama-3.1-8b-instruct
region: us-east
metric: p95_latency_ms
current: 412 ms
baseline: 330 ms (rolling median, 7d)
delta: +24.8%
window: 15m
min_samples: 240 (ok)
labels: source=perf-canary, scheduler_mode=stable, runtime_build=runtime-1.14.0-rc3, kernel_id=fa2_gemm_v17
links: grafana=https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/perf-canary/model?var-model=llama-3.1-8b-instruct&var-region=us-east | runbook=https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/perf-canary-triage
notes: deploy_window_suppression=false

Sean Gallagher: got it in PagerDuty, looks good overall. 2 quick things:
1) can we include the *git SHA* for runtime? `runtime_build` is helpful but not enough when we’re correlating w/ deploys/PRs.
2) i don’t see GPU SKU anywhere. need `gpu_sku` in the alert body so the first responder doesn’t have to click through 3 dashboards.

Tomáš Novák: +1 on gpu sku. also if we have it, node pool / capacity tier would help (dedicated vs hosted). but sku is the big one.

Allison Grant: from standards POV: the allowed alert fields are fine, but we should make sure `gpu_sku` is also a metric label so it can be a first-class filter in grafana. alert payload can include it as a rendered field.

Logan Wright: checking ingestion side: we *do* have `gpu_sku` on a bunch of runtime metrics, but i think perf-canary is still missing it on the canary request tags. if the request never propagates it, the aggregation can’t attach it.

Nadia Rahman: fwiw the label schema doc currently has `gpu_sku` as “optional slice” w/ budgeted cardinality, but for canary it’s expected. we negotiated that specifically bc fleet heterogeneity was a known risk.

Omar El-Sayed: runtime side: can confirm we’re emitting `runtime_build` + `scheduler_mode` today. we also have `runtime_git_sha` available in the process metadata, but it’s not currently being attached to the canary metrics event.

Rafael Mendes: super helpful. for the alert body, what exact fields do folks want? thinking:
- `runtime_version` (human)
- `runtime_git_sha` (full or short?)
- `gpu_sku`
- (maybe) `cluster`/`pool`

Sean Gallagher: short sha is fine in the pager text (7 chars), but include full sha in the dashboard link params if possible. mostly i want to be able to grep deploy logs quickly.

Tomáš Novák: +1. also can we ensure the runbook link goes directly to the “what to do first” section anchor? current link lands at top.

Allison Grant: if we include SHA, name it consistently: `runtime_sha` (string) not `git_sha` in one place and `runtime_git_sha` in another. telemetry gets messy fast.

Logan Wright: +1 on consistent naming. also: make sure we don’t add both `runtime_sha` and `runtime_build` as separate *labels* if we don’t need it. SHA as an *alert field* is fine; as a metric label it’s too high-cardinality.

Nadia Rahman: strongly agree: SHA should not be a metric label. render it in alert payload via deploy annotation lookup, or attach as non-indexed field in logs/traces.

Rafael Mendes: ok, action items i’m taking:
1) add `gpu_sku` to alert body (and confirm it’s present as metric label on the timeseries)
2) add `runtime_sha` (short) to alert body via deploy annotation mapping, not as a label
3) tweak runbook link to anchor

Omar El-Sayed: i’ll sync w/ Marcus/Omar (me) on propagation. likely we just need to ensure the canary request context includes `gpu_sku` tag from router -> metrics emitter.

Sean Gallagher: also: the “labels:” line in the alert currently prints `kernel_id` which is good. can we add `kernel_fallback_reason` when present? might be empty for most.

Rafael Mendes: noted. i’ll keep that as optional field (only show when non-empty) so we don’t spam.

incident-bot: Acknowledged by Rafael Mendes (test alert)

Tomáš Novák: everything else looks solid. dedup key working? i only got one PD notification.

Rafael Mendes: yeah dedup seems ok: `perf-canary|p95_latency|model|region|scheduler_mode|gpu_sku` (once gpu is there). for the test it was missing sku so it fell back to `unknown`.

Allison Grant: please make sure the fallback value is exactly `unknown` (not empty) so dashboards don’t create a separate “null” bucket.

Logan Wright: +1. we’ve been burned by `(none)` vs empty string before.

Sean Gallagher: cool. once gpu sku + sha are in, i’m happy to flip from “test paging” to “ticket-only” in phase 1 until we tune thresholds.

Rafael Mendes: 👍 i’ll post an update when the next test fires w/ the new fields.
